name: Bleeding-Heart Libertarianism
summary: Bleeding-heart libertarianism is a libertarian current, associated with the Arizona School, that holds that civil liberties and free markets are justified in part by how well they serve the poor and disadvantaged. It treats property rights as important but not absolute, accepts some limited safety net such as a negative income tax or targeted basic income, and opposes state-propped privilege, drug prohibition, war and border restrictions. It embraces a Rawls-influenced notion of social justice applied to the institutional system as a whole, while pursuing it through markets rather than a standing redistributive apparatus.
scope: The contemporary philosophical movement of the 2010s centered on the Bleeding Heart Libertarians blog and the Arizona School (Zwolinski, Tomasi, Schmidtz, Gaus, Vallier, Brennan, Tesón, Long, Chartier), drawing on Hayek, Friedman and classical liberals. Excludes strict Rothbardian or Randian property absolutism, and answers on topics the sources never take up (most non-economic items) are inferred from its civil-liberties and pro-market principles.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Hayek and Friedman allow a state safety net, but a full state-guaranteed system goes beyond the targeted help these libertarians favor; inferred from that.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Authors on the blog argue against wage regulations, treating the working poor as better served by open labor markets than by statutory wage floors.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The blog's mission calls the flourishing of free markets practically and morally important, and the lead essay argues capitalism does best by the least well-off.

public-ownership.rationale: Their case for free markets as the system that serves the poorest leaves no room for state ownership of whole industries.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Mises objected to progressive taxes and Rothbard held tax cuts help lower incomes most; this lane is inferred from that rather than stated about wealth taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Voluntary unions fit a libertarian concern for workers, and left-leaning strands value them, though sources here say little; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: They agree individual property rights matter greatly but explicitly deny that they are moral absolutes, so adherents lean to agree without strong force.

regulate-corporations.rationale: They blame much corporate advantage on state favors and want the privileges removed, not more regulation added; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Zwolinski concedes much existing welfare is harmful but does not support removing all welfare, and the lead essay rejects only the redistributive apparatus as a requirement.

worker-ownership.rationale: Voluntary worker ownership is permitted but nothing in the sources has them wanting workers to collectively own firms; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Civil liberties are a stated pillar of the view, so adherents would resist terror surveillance; applied by inference as the sources never discuss it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The movement joins support for civil liberties with free markets, and bloggers argue against paternalistic regulation of what adults ingest.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: A movement built on civil liberties would reject legal limits on speech, though the sources do not discuss hate speech itself.

strong-leader.rationale: Adherents want power constrained, as in the call to criticize every form of state power; the statement is inferred to be rejected.

state-harmful.rationale: The view criticizes state power in every form yet accepts a limited state and a safety net, so adherents mostly disagree with calling it unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Civil-libertarian outlook suggests opposing strict limits, but the sources never mention guns; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: A view that wants all state power criticized would not grant police and military more authority; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Part of the civil-liberties and anti-paternalist package; inferred since no source names sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: Libertarians generally prefer smaller, closer government but the sources do not address this; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: Concern for disadvantaged people leads to preferring rehabilitation over punishment; inferred rather than stated.

traditional-family.rationale: SEP places right-libertarians with social conservatism as the opposite pole, so bleeding-heart adherents typically do not endorse this; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Support for civil liberties and social tolerance is part of how the movement defines itself against social conservatism.

abortion-legal.rationale: Fits the civil-liberties side of the view, though adherents differ and sources are silent; inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nothing in the movement favors expanding religion in public life; inferred from its liberal social outlook.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Concern for the disadvantaged is central, and adherents blame state-propped injustice, but active policy is not specified; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The movement takes no stand on this philosophical question; adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The view is individualist and cosmopolitan, so protecting national culture is not a priority; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: The lead essay urges a return to classical liberal ideas but sources say nothing about pace of change, and adherents range from reformers to radicals; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Contributors write on the libertarian case for open borders, so adherents reject cutting immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Distrust of concentrated state power suggests resisting stronger international bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: The movement holds free markets benefit the poor most, citing Mises and Rothbard, and supports markets generally.

nation-first.rationale: Their openness to immigrants and a global moral view suggests rejecting nation-first policy; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Some contributors back intervention for human rights while others stress anti-war liberty; adherents are split.

open-borders.rationale: Contributors such as Javier Hidalgo have published The Libertarian Case for Open Borders and the blog lists open borders as a research interest.

limit-growth.rationale: They defend capitalism by what growth does for the poor, so limiting growth would clash; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Skeptical of state action, though they favor some pricing schemes; the sources do not address climate, so inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Their argument that free markets steadily improve the lot of the poorest implies optimism about progress, but technology is never discussed; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Pro-market and pro-technology orientation suggests support; inferred, as no source mentions nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: They advance their case by essays, blogs and persuasion in debates like the Cato Unbound exchange, so revolution is not part of their method; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Jason Brennan has argued for epistocracy, but most adherents resist rule by experts; adherents are divided.

central-planning.rationale: They defend free markets as best for the least well-off and reject planning by the state.

socialized-markets.rationale: Private ownership is the default they defend, though worker-owned firms are allowed voluntarily; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Zwolinski draws on Henry George for a land-based dividend, but replacing most taxes is not his claim.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Libertarian leaning against heavy taxation, though neoclassical liberals accept some redistribution; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Zwolinski argues a basic income is defensible on libertarian grounds but prefers a targeted version to a fully universal one; adherents are divided.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Free trade is part of the market case they make for the poor, and they oppose state favors to industries.

state-directs-investment.rationale: They criticize state-propped privilege and defend market allocation, so directed investment is rejected.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources stress property and contract but not any preference for small owners; adherents differ.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Their defense of capitalism rests on benefits to lowest paid workers, which presupposes wage labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Libertarians differ on money; some like Hayek favored competing currencies, others tolerate central banks; split.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The lead essay favors outcomes arising through property and contract, which excludes state-recognized bodies that fix wages for whole sectors.

one-party-rule.rationale: The movement is defined by civil liberties alongside free markets, which a state led by one ideological party would deny.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Liberal-individualist outlook weighs against monarchy, though it is not a central issue; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: Some adherents like Jason Brennan are openly skeptical of democracy while others accept it; split.

direct-votes.rationale: Libertarian-leaning scholars distrust majorities overriding individual rights, and Brennan is openly skeptical of democracy; inferred for referendums.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power conflict with their market-based view; inferred.

right-to-secede.rationale: Libertarian ideas of consent and exit favor allowing regions to leave, but the sources do not address secession; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: The view holds that institutions should be judged by how they serve the poorest and rejects ruling classes.

political-violence-never.rationale: Adherents differ on whether any political violence is justified; not addressed by sources.

war-builds-character.rationale: Source notes the movement ties warfare to state-propped class crime, so glorifying war is rejected.

separate-church-state.rationale: A civil-liberties stance that defines itself against social conservatism points toward strict separation; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: They define themselves against social conservatism and favor civil liberties.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Roderick Long and others support private provision while many contributors defend a limited state; split.

military-superiority.rationale: Anti-war and anti-state-power stance suggests rejecting military primacy; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Contributors argue for open borders and equal concern for all, so ethnic nationhood is rejected.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Left-leaning contributors use class analysis of state privilege while others do not; split.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Lead essay says inequality is acceptable if the system benefits the lowest paid, which rejects outcome equality as the goal.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Lockean proviso and property claims cut both ways here; adherents are divided.

colonial-reparations.rationale: They oppose redistribution as a standing system, though rectification is permitted in Nozick's theory; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Contributors argue for open borders and individual rights, which leaves no basis for political unity by civilization; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rand treated self-interest as virtue, but bleeding-heart authors stress concern for others; split.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The movement is a rights-based liberalism built on individual liberty, so community duties ranking above rights is rejected.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses environmental ethics, and adherents range from pro-conservation to indifferent; split.

limit-population.rationale: Coercive limits on childbearing would violate the individual liberty they defend; inferred from that.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They defend capitalism by what it does for the worst off, which includes industrial growth.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Their pro-market stance tends to welcome innovation even when it disrupts incumbents, though the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Authors who argue against paternalistic regulation of adults' choices would extend that to enhancement; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Their distrust of expanding state discretion suggests skepticism of handing decisions to algorithms; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Privacy from the state follows from their civil-liberties commitments, though sources do not mention encryption; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement positions itself against social conservatism and favors liberty-based reform, not restoring a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Arizona School is described as observation-based and empirically accountable.

direct-action.rationale: The movement works through writing and debate rather than street tactics; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: The sources never take up this question of prefigurative politics, and adherents have no shared view; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Their defense of capitalism rests on its material gains for the least well-off, which a foraging life would forgo.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Market exchange and specialization are central to their defense of capitalism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: They accept inequality if the system benefits the worst-off and reject need-based distribution as a principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Their view defends production for profit in markets as best serving consumers and the poor, citing Mises.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Lead essay cites Mises that entrepreneurs' interests never diverge from consumers and sees markets benefiting workers.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Class dictatorship contradicts both the civil liberties and equal rights the movement affirms.

collective-farming.rationale: Their property-and-contract approach to justice rejects compelling farmers into collectives.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Some left-leaning writers blame state-capitalist ties for war, but most reject the claim; contested among adherents.

taxation-theft.rationale: Zwolinski calls the view that all state transfers are theft hard to defend, so most adherents disagree.

harm-principle.rationale: Civil-liberties libertarian stance tracks the harm principle, though the sources do not state it directly.

individual-rights-only.rationale: An individualist liberalism gives rights to persons, though group rights are not discussed in the sources; inferred.

conscription.rationale: Forced service treats persons as means and conflicts with self-ownership, which libertarians defend; inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Some libertarians prize exit as the main check on power, but the sources do not take a side; adherents differ.

state-as-business.rationale: The idea of citizens as customers appeals to some libertarians but others object; the sources are silent, so split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Zwolinski's freedom argument says dependence on employers undermines freedom, but this is one author's view; adherents differ.

media-academia-power.rationale: The movement itself is rooted in universities and does not complain of academic power; inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Their stated concern for the worst-off and equal moral standing makes genetic racial ranking unwelcome; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and corporate bodies conflicts with their individualism; inferred.

total-state.rationale: A state directing every area of life is the opposite of the limited-government liberalism they hold.

national-rebirth.rationale: Radical national renewal sits poorly with a cosmopolitan, open-borders individualism; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Their critique of state power and state-propped warfare, as in Doherty's remark, rejects expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority resting on personal oaths conflicts with impersonal rule of law and equal rights; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Legally bound labor violates self-ownership and free contract, the basis of their view.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: The Arizona School aims to be empirically accountable, which sits poorly with this claim; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Rights-based moral philosophy typically assumes universal moral truths; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: The Arizona school and Zwolinski's pluralism favor many views of the good rather than one fixed good; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No source covers this and libertarian-leaning thinkers hold varied views on national states; split.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Their open-borders view favors broad movement rights, but a special right of return is not discussed; split.

revive-national-language.rationale: State programs to revive a language conflict with individual choice, though the question is not discussed; inferred.

workplace-democracy.rationale: They leave firm governance to voluntary contract, so a mandated public vote is unlikely to appeal; inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Wikipedia links the Arizona School to Milton Friedman's school voucher ideas.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Libertarian-leaning economists differ on deficits and stimulus, and none of the sources decide it; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Their combination of free markets and civil liberties suggests the two reinforce each other, but the sources do not state it; inferred.

rule-by-example.rationale: Governing by rulers' moral example instead of law conflicts with the rule-of-law emphasis; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers differ on the nation-state and the sources never address it; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Skepticism of war and state power suggests discomfort with unilateral force, though some contributors back humanitarian intervention; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The sources do not address the relation of reason and faith, and adherents include believers and secularists; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: With open borders as a leading cause, adherents would not restrict benefits by citizenship; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Zwolinski prefers a negative income tax or targeted grant, with no work test mentioned; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Mises-style harmony of interests (cited in the lead essay) appeals to some, while left-libertarians stress class conflict; split.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nothing in the movement suggests destroying inherited institutions for new creation; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: A bloc built on shared grievance against Western powers has no basis in their liberal individualism; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Class organization along national lines is alien to their individualism; inferred.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Legal sex roles conflict with equal rights before the law and with civil liberties, which the movement affirms.

ban-interest.rationale: Their free-market and contract-based justification of capitalism leaves no place for a legal ban on interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Legal racial separation contradicts the equal rights and civil liberties on which the movement is built.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Brian Doherty and Roderick Long see the state used by the well-off, yet others do not; adherents differ.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Market-friendly views might favor production, but environmental concern splits adherents and no source discusses it; split.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Contributors defend open borders and tolerance, so demanding that immigrants give up their culture is unlikely; inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy about elites engineering immigration is not part of the movement's reasoning; inferred.

proportional-representation.rationale: Electoral systems are not a concern in the sources, and adherents have no common view; split.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a government form abroad conflicts with their anti-war, anti-state-power outlook; inferred.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The movement's social-justice side may accept some structural claims while market-focused members reject them; split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Their critique of crony capitalism and state-propped privilege fits a view that political elites serve themselves; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State prevention of births by people with heritable defects violates the basic liberty and equal worth they affirm.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Their rights-protecting stance would favor legal accountability for abuses, though not stated; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Hayek and Friedman allowed a safety net and Zwolinski backs some redistribution, so they reject a strictly minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Discouraging marriage across racial lines contradicts the equal moral standing and liberty the movement affirms.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Concern for the worst-off and civil liberties for all, as Wikipedia describes the movement, presupposes equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The question of socialism in one country is not a concern for the movement, and adherents hold no view on it; split.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The sources do not address settler colonialism and adherents differ on how property claims apply; split.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Equal law for everyone fits a liberal commitment to equal rights, though the sources do not address it; inferred.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Legal limits on conversion violate the civil liberties that define the movement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A ban on slaughter imposes a religious norm by law, against civil liberties and free markets.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Their civil-liberties outlook favors neutral state schools, though many prefer vouchers over state schooling; inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: They criticize every form of state power and would not endorse a state growing stronger.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Consent-based legitimacy is the usual liberal and libertarian view, though no source states it here; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: The mercantilist goal of exporting more than importing contradicts their free-trade reasoning; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcing or pressuring a minority to leave violates the individual rights at the core of the view.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: SEP notes Zwolinski criticizes non-aggression-principle approaches while Long is closer to absolutism; adherents split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The statement is about struggle between peoples, which they reject; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Free speech and association suggest resistance to banning parties, though sources do not discuss it; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Zwolinski invokes a republican idea of liberty to argue dependence on employers undermines freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: Their wish to criticize every form of state power fits checks among separate bodies; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined vanguard directing workers conflicts with the pluralism and voluntary association they hold.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The lead essay says the fate of the lowest paid is essential to capitalism's justification and embraces social justice measured by their position.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Broader private ownership matches their market stance, though no source mentions housing policy; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voluntary association suggests they would resist legal limits on strikes, though they dislike coercive picketing too; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: They hold that institutions explain poverty and social justice concerns the institutional system.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contributors who defend open borders reject the claim that diversity undermines society; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not a theme of the movement and cuts against their stress on accountable institutions; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Suspending legal protections contradicts the civil liberties that define the movement.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Their case is that free markets serve the least well-off best, so price ceilings on food are rejected.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government control of media contradicts the civil liberties at the movement's core.

party-commands-army.rationale: Subordinating the state's army to a party contradicts constitutional, limited government.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: A movement defending open borders would not favor long waits for citizenship; inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay rules for legislators are not discussed; inferred from their general pro-market outlook.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding party discipline conflicts with individualism, though sources do not discuss it; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers welcome free movement but distrust supranational bureaucracy, and no source decides it; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: A limited-government outlook favors dividing control over force; inferred.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the movement's concern, and adherents have no common view; split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars contradicts civil liberties and equal rights, the basis of the movement.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The movement is anti-war, but working for one's own government's defeat is a tactic it never endorses; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Censorship of art violates the civil liberties that the movement defends.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Their wish to limit state power suggests wariness of unlimited tenure; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Accountability of officials fits their limited-government outlook; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Skepticism of war and state-propped military power suggests favoring withdrawal; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Banning rentals contradicts the property rights and market exchange they defend.

people-in-arms.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers differ on militias versus professional forces and sources do not say; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The claim is about moral value of a way of life, which a pluralist liberal view would not endorse; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The movement has no stance on national reunification, and adherents differ; split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement is itself academic and does not share this populist claim; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The question of ranking cultures is not addressed, and adherents differ in cosmopolitan and pluralist ways; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Distrust of state power suggests wariness about state executions, though the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers disagree about state school curricula and the sources do not address it; split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Mandated religious teaching in public schools contradicts the movement's secular civil-liberties stance.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Legal limits on pornography between adults conflict with the movement's civil liberties.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: A movement favoring open borders would not want citizenship tied to descent; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: State funding of language programs is unlikely to appeal to them, though sources are silent; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers differ over exemptions from general laws, and no source decides it; split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: This is a Millian liberal view that fits their commitment to individual liberty, though not stated in the sources; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Contract-respecting libertarians resist cancellation, though concern for the poor pulls the other way; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Their reform program works through property, contract and market institutions rather than wholesale transformation of the property system; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Procedure for rewriting constitutions is not addressed, and adherents have no shared view; split.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Giving up political freedoms for growth contradicts the combination of liberty and market that defines the view.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Zwolinski reportedly favored a global basic income in ideal conditions, but adherents differ on state aid.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Their skepticism of military power suggests resisting national nuclear arsenals; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: This constitutional choice is not discussed, and adherents have no shared view; split.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers range from abolishing central banks to accepting independent ones, and no source decides it; split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The movement's anti-war outlook weighs against refusing territorial compromise; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Lead essay says classical liberals valued property partly for the poor but denies property is a mere instrument; adherents differ.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The question is a matter of Marxist classification that the movement does not address, and adherents differ; split.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Their market and tort-based outlook resists acting without proof of harm; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Anti-war contributors dislike alliances while others accept defensive pacts, and the sources do not decide; split.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: A consent-based view of authority would call annexation without consent unlawful; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Curbing churches' property and clergy by state power contradicts civil liberties and property rights.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not a concern of the movement; split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Their consent-based outlook opposes using force to keep regions in; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Decentralization and experimentation fit their view that communities may differ; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A sacred, divine-descent ruler contradicts liberal individualism and equal standing.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Mises objected to progressive taxes while Hayek and Friedman allowed a safety net funded by taxes, so adherents differ; split.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-versus-nurture question is not addressed by the movement, and adherents hold both views; split.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: A ruler not bound by law contradicts the limited government and rule of law they uphold.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is outside the movement's concerns, and adherents hold no common view; split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical mixed-constitution idea is not discussed, and adherents hold no shared view; split.

leader-cult.rationale: Mass praise for a national leader is incompatible with the movement's skepticism of state power.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are not addressed, and adherents hold varied views; split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The statement concerns Marxist theory that the movement does not address, and adherents hold no view; split.

land-redistribution.rationale: Zwolinski's Georgist idea is a small land-based dividend and not seizure of estates, so adherents lean against redistribution of land; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Their stress on free movement and individual property suggests supporting return of those expelled; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claiming territory because co-nationals live there rests on ethnic collectivism that the individualist view rejects.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion contradicts the civil liberties the movement defends.

women-must-cover.rationale: A legal requirement to cover contradicts the civil liberties the movement defends.

common-currency.rationale: Libertarian-leaning thinkers differ on monetary unions, and the sources do not address it; split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The movement opposes border restrictions and nationalism, so tying patriotism to a politics for workers is inferred to be disliked.

material-over-identity.rationale: An intra-left debate; the sources show no position, and the movement stresses both economic and civil-liberty concerns.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Single-party rule contradicts the movement's civil-liberties commitments, and it favours markets under limited government, not under a party.

missingStatements.text: A just economic system should be judged mainly by how well it treats its least well-off members.
missingStatements.rationale: The lead essay makes the fate of the lowest paid workers essential to capitalism's justification and embraces Rawls-style social justice.

missingStatements.text: Governments should not give special legal privileges to well-connected businesses.
missingStatements.rationale: Reason's summary cites Doherty and Long on state-propped class advantage and Rothbard on crony capitalists feeding at the public trough.

notes: Contributors disagree on a basic income, open borders details, humanitarian intervention and private provision of defense. Many answers on non-economic topics are inferred from the movement's civil-liberties and pro-market commitments.
